annotation.authors_or_issuer: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), U.S. Department of Transportation
annotation.venue: Code of Federal Regulations, 14 CFR Part 89
annotation.summary_en: US FAA regulation (14 CFR Part 89) requiring remote identification of unmanned aircraft. It sets operating requirements, broadcast message elements, performance standards, FAA-recognized identification areas, means-of-compliance and declaration-of-compliance procedures, and producer obligations such as audits, labeling, and defect notification.
key_provisions_or_claims: After Sept 16, 2023, UAS operations in US airspace must use standard Remote ID or a broadcast module, or operate within FAA-recognized identification areas.
Standard Remote ID aircraft must broadcast identity, location, altitude, velocity, and emergency status, and be unable to take off if the equipment is not functional.
Producers must obtain FAA acceptance of a declaration of compliance based on an accepted means of compliance.
Producers must undergo independent audits, FAA inspection, labeling, and defect notification within 15 days.
Foreign-registered UAS operators must submit a notice of identification and obtain a Confirmation of Identification.
